title: Fast and slow
summary: Learn the Italian words for speed and the ones that speed up or slow down.

hook.text: Film composers pick the speed first: a chase never crawls, and a lullaby never races. Press play to hear a tune at a slow, sleepy speed. If it ran twice as fast, what would change?

explore.text: Choose one key. Tap it in a slow, steady pulse, like a gentle walk. Now speed up gradually, a little faster with every tap, until the taps almost blur. Then slow down gradually until you are back to a walk.
explore.goal: Tap a key slowly, then speed up gradually, then slow down gradually.

cards.text: Speed words are Italian and sit at the start of a piece. They tell you the [[tempo|tempo]]. [[lento|Lento]] means slow. [[adagio|Adagio]] means slow and calm. [[andante|Andante]] means at a walking pace. Press play to hear a slow, calm speed.

Moving up: [[moderato|moderato]] means a moderate speed. [[allegretto|Allegretto]] means quite quick. [[allegro|Allegro]] means quick and lively. Put [[poco|poco]] (a little) or [[molto|molto]] (very much) in front to adjust: *molto allegro* is very quick.

Speed can change inside a piece. [[accelerando|Accelerando]] (*accel.*) means gradually faster. [[ritardando|Ritardando]] (*rit.*) and [[rallentando|rallentando]] (*rall.*) mean gradually slower. [[a-tempo|A tempo]] means back to the original speed. *Poco rit.* is a little slower.

alternative.text: Picture a day out. You shuffle out of bed: [[lento|lento]]. A calm stroll: [[adagio|adagio]]. Walking to school: [[andante|andante]]. Hurrying so you are not late: [[allegro|allegro]]. Running faster and faster: [[accelerando|accelerando]]. Tiring, you slow: [[ritardando|ritardando]]. Then you settle back to your normal walk: [[a-tempo|a tempo]].

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **allegro**?
questions.hint: Allegro means quick and lively. Tap along: which clip makes you tap faster?

options.reason: Clip A is slow, about one beat a second. [[allegro|Allegro]] is quick and lively, which is clip B.

questions.prompt: Which Italian word means **at a walking pace**?
questions.hint: Picture someone strolling along. Is that slower or quicker than quick and lively?

options.reason: [[adagio|Adagio]] is slow and calm, slower than a walk. At a walking pace is [[andante|andante]].
[[allegro|Allegro]] is quick and lively, quicker than walking. At a walking pace is [[andante|andante]].

questions.prompt: Put these words in order, from slowest to fastest.
questions.hint: Start with the slow and calm one. Allegro is quick and lively, so where does it go?

payload.reason: Slowest to fastest: [[adagio|adagio]] slow and calm, [[andante|andante]] walking pace, [[moderato|moderato]] moderate, [[allegro|allegro]] quick and lively.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.hint: Accelerando and a tempo are about change. Adagio is about a fixed speed.

left.reason: [[accelerando|Accelerando]] speeds up gradually: it gets faster, not slower.
[[ritardando|Ritardando]] slows down gradually. It is the opposite of accelerando.
[[a-tempo|A tempo]] means return to the original speed, after a change.
[[adagio|Adagio]] is a fixed slow, calm speed, not a change.

questions.hint: Molto changes the word after it. Is it a little, or very much?

options.reason: [[poco|Poco]] means a little. [[molto|Molto]] is the opposite: very much, so *molto allegro* is very quick.
Slow and calm is [[adagio|adagio]]. [[allegro|Allegro]] is quick, and [[molto|molto]] makes it even quicker.

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **adagio**: slow and calm?
questions.hint: Tap a steady beat. Which clip gives you plenty of time between taps?

options.reason: Clip B is quick: about two beats a second. [[adagio|Adagio]] is slow and calm, which is clip A.

questions.prompt: Put these words in order, from slowest to fastest.
questions.hint: Lento is the slow one. Allegro is the quick and lively one. Place the others between.

payload.reason: Slowest to fastest: [[lento|lento]] slow, [[moderato|moderato]] moderate, [[allegretto|allegretto]] quite quick, [[allegro|allegro]] quick and lively.

questions.prompt: Which word means **go back to the original speed**?
questions.hint: Two of these words are about changing speed. One is about returning.

options.reason: [[ritardando|Ritardando]] means gradually slower. Going back to the original speed is [[a-tempo|a tempo]].
[[accelerando|Accelerando]] means gradually faster. Going back to the original speed is [[a-tempo|a tempo]].

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.hint: Walking is andante. Moderate sits in the middle. Allegro is lively.

left.reason: [[moderato|Moderato]] is a moderate speed: not slow, not quick.

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **andante**: a walking pace?
questions.hint: Tap your feet as if you were strolling. Which clip fits a stroll, not a jog?

options.reason: Clip B is much quicker than a walk: more like a jog. [[andante|Andante]] is a walking pace, which is clip A.

questions.hint: It sits in front of another word, as in *poco rit.*

options.reason: Very much is [[molto|molto]]. [[poco|Poco]] is the opposite: a little.
Half is [[mezzo|mezzo]], which you met with volume. [[poco|Poco]] means a little.

questions.prompt: Match each short form to its full word.
questions.hint: Each short form starts with the first letters of its word.

left.reason: *rall.* is short for [[rallentando|rallentando]]: gradually slower, and often broader.

questions.hint: Gradually faster is a change in speed. One of these is a fixed speed.

options.reason: [[ritardando|Ritardando]] means gradually slower. The word for gradually faster is [[accelerando|accelerando]].
[[allegretto|Allegretto]] is a fixed speed: quite quick. It does not change gradually. Gradually faster is [[accelerando|accelerando]].

questions.prompt: Put these words in order, from slowest to fastest.
questions.hint: Walking pace sits between slow and calm, and quick and lively.

payload.reason: Slowest to fastest: [[adagio|adagio]] slow and calm, [[andante|andante]] walking pace, [[allegro|allegro]] quick and lively.

questions.hint: Both words are about a change. Does the music speed up or slow down?

options.reason: Back to the original speed is [[a-tempo|a tempo]]. [[ritardando|Ritardando]] and [[rallentando|rallentando]] both ask for a gradual slowing.
Gradually faster is [[accelerando|accelerando]]. [[ritardando|Ritardando]] and [[rallentando|rallentando]] go the other way.

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **allegro**: quick and lively?
questions.hint: Which clip makes you want to move faster?

options.reason: Clip B is slow: about one beat a second. [[allegro|Allegro]] is quick and lively, which is clip A.

questions.prompt: Which of these words asks for the **quickest** speed?
questions.hint: Allegretto means quite quick. Which word means quick and lively?

options.reason: [[allegretto|Allegretto]] is quite quick, but slower than allegro.
[[moderato|Moderato]] is a moderate speed, not a quick one.

points: [[lento|Lento]] and [[adagio|adagio]] are slow. Then, getting faster: [[andante|andante]] (walking pace), [[moderato|moderato]] (moderate), [[allegretto|allegretto]] (quite quick), [[allegro|allegro]] (quick and lively).
[[poco|Poco]] means a little and [[molto|molto]] means very much: *molto allegro* is very quick.
[[accelerando|Accelerando]] gets gradually faster. [[ritardando|Ritardando]] and [[rallentando|rallentando]] get gradually slower. [[a-tempo|A tempo]] goes back to the original speed.
